experiment: Black-box fuzzing of a firmware CMP web-configuration pipeline
method: Authenticated same-origin HTTP POST directly to the *.mwp endpoints, bypassing browser-side JavaScript validation to exercise the firmware server-side input validation. Each payload sent with pageMode=bufferwrite (validate) and the field restored to baseline afterwards.

key_protocol_facts.pageMode: bufferwrite validates and stages the value (server returns resp=OK/ERROR); flush commits the staged buffer. Fuzzing used bufferwrite only, so malformed values were validated but never persisted.

stability.note: Recurring HTTP 503 / ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING observed only under back-to-back sub-500ms submits; eliminated with a >=450 ms inter-request delay. No payload caused a crash or hang.

CRITICAL_format_string_CWE134.where: trace/dump logging path (shared trace function / CMP_print) shared by all CMP fields
CRITICAL_format_string_CWE134.observation: The %x%x%n specifiers were INTERPRETED (%x%x -> stack leak; %n -> memory write), proving a user-controlled field reaches a printf-family FORMAT position in the logging/dump path.
CRITICAL_format_string_CWE134.impact: Information disclosure (%x/%s leak memory) and memory corruption / potential crash or RCE (%n).
CRITICAL_format_string_CWE134.root_cause: CMP_print(bio, userValue) — user data passed as the format string.
CRITICAL_format_string_CWE134.fix: CMP_print(bio, "%s", userValue) — enforce a fixed format specifier in the shared trace function; fixes ALL fields at once without touching per-field validation.
CRITICAL_format_string_CWE134.note: Discovered by empirical fuzzing; NOT captured by the design-based analysis, which correctly ruled out only shell injection.

path_fields_validation_decision.decision: INTENTIONALLY PERMISSIVE — do NOT add content validation to Certificate Path / Revoke Path.
path_fields_validation_decision.rationale: These are remote-server URL path components (e.g. https://host:port/<path>), not a local filesystem or shell boundary. Traversal/metacharacters are inert literal argv elements. Constraining them would break legitimate server paths without a security benefit.

CmpServerAddr_1.length_bound: 100 characters ('Domain Name length cannot exceed 100 characters')
CmpServerAddr_1.oversize_4096: HTTP 400 (handled at HTTP layer, not app validation)
CmpServerAddr_1.nul_behavior: C-string truncation: 'A\x00B' -> 'A', '1.2.3.4\x00;reboot' -> '1.2.3.4' (post-NUL content DISCARDED, not forwarded -> no injection bypass)

CmpServerPort_1.issue: NO range check: out-of-range port values (<=0, >65535, and 11-digit) are accepted; format is validated but numeric range is not.

permissive_fields.note: These fields enforce ONLY a length bound (reject at ~1024, accept 256). Content is NOT semantically filtered: command-injection metacharacters, path-traversal sequences, format-string specifiers, NUL, and unicode are all ACCEPTED at validation time.
permissive_fields.exploitability_assessment: Despite permissive field-level validation, these values are (a) passed via the in-memory argc/argv construction as discrete arguments with NO shell invoked, and (b) used as remote-URL path components / protocol fields, not local filesystem paths. Command injection and local file access are therefore prevented BY CONSTRUCTION, consistent with the paper's core thesis. The format-string specifiers (%s/%n) reaching a later logged CMP transaction warrant a dedicated run-time check.

credential_file_upload_path.target: CMP private-key upload slot via the web-management Load&Save > HTTP page (endpoint POST /loadandsave_http.mwp?pageMode=action&button=<key-upload-button>&isupload=true, multipart/form-data)
credential_file_upload_path.method: Uploaded 51 malformed/oversized/wrong-type/injection-laced key files (a PEM text corpus, a binary DER/ASN.1 corpus, a wrong-PEM-object-type corpus, and a PEM-marker-syntax and non-key-file-type corpus) through the same-origin authenticated upload widget (setInputFiles + change event). Read the firmware verdict dialog for each and verified device liveness (dashboard responsive, clock advancing) after every upload. A valid key was used as a positive control.

corpus_results.der_lenoverflow.der (9 B, ASN.1 SEQUENCE: File load operation failed (no allocation DoS)
corpus_results.der_deepnest.der (8000 B, 2000-level ind: File load operation failed (no stack overflow)
corpus_results.xml_xxe.xml (XML with external-entity XX: File load operation failed (no file disclosure)
corpus_results.shebang.pem (#!/bin/sh; reboot; rm -rf /: File was successfully loaded (ACCEPTED; preamble skipped, commands inert)
corpus_results.key.pem (valid control): File was successfully loaded (accepted); a later re-upload of the identical key returned 'load operation failed' as an expected duplicate/already-present rejection

layered_validation_observed.File validation failed: early structural/content pre-check rejects empty, header-only, truncated, non-key, NUL-bearing, CRLF/log-injection, and metacharacter/format-string-laden inputs before any key parse
layered_validation_observed.Data malformed: PEM envelope inspected but the BEGIN/END framing is malformed
layered_validation_observed.File load operation failed: input passed the framing checks but the key parse/decode (base64/ASN.1), BOM prefix, mid-body NUL, or decrypt step failed
layered_validation_observed.File oversized: a dedicated size/line-length guard rejects an over-long single base64 line (200 KB) before parsing

notable_behaviors.multi_key_pem_accepted: doublekey.pem (two valid PEM keys concatenated) was ACCEPTED ('File was successfully loaded') -- the parser tolerates a multi-object PEM and uses the first key. This is lenient input handling rather than a vulnerability (both objects are the same valid key), but a defence-in-depth improvement would be to reject or explicitly warn on files containing more than one private key.
notable_behaviors.format_string_file_rejected: fmt_body.pem (pure '%n%s%x%p' body) and metachars.pem were both rejected at validation, confirming the upload path does not forward file content to any printf-family format position (unlike the text config field CWE-134 defect).
notable_behaviors.log_injection_rejected: crlf_inject.pem (embedded CRLF + fake '[CRITICAL] ... reboot now' log lines) was rejected at validation -> no CRLF/log-injection surface via the key file.
notable_behaviors.oversize_line_guard: overlong_line.pem produced a distinct 'File oversized' verdict, showing an explicit size guard separate from the parse path.
notable_behaviors.asn1_dos_resistant: der_lenoverflow.der (SEQUENCE header claiming a 4 GB body) and der_deepnest.der (2000-level indefinite-length ASN.1) were both rejected with 'File load operation failed' and caused no allocation blow-up, stack overflow, or crash -> the DER/ASN.1 parser is length- and depth-bounded.
notable_behaviors.wrong_object_type_rejected: A certificate (BEGIN CERTIFICATE) and a CSR (BEGIN CERTIFICATE REQUEST) placed in the key slot were rejected -> the slot enforces the expected object type.
notable_behaviors.trailing_leading_garbage_rejected: A valid key with junk appended after END, and junk prepended before a valid key, were both rejected ('File load operation failed') -> stricter than the concatenated-two-keys case; trailing/leading data is not silently ignored.
notable_behaviors.encoding_rejected: UTF-16LE-encoded key and a 400000-blank-line file were rejected without DoS -> encoding and line-count are bounded.
notable_behaviors.private_key_type_enforced: Wrong key classes and formats were rejected: PUBLIC KEY, RSA PUBLIC KEY, DSA PRIVATE KEY, OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY (validation failed) and PGP PRIVATE KEY BLOCK, DH PARAMETERS (load failed). The slot enforces an RSA/EC PRIVATE KEY object, not merely 'any PEM'.
notable_behaviors.marker_syntax_strict: PEM-marker syntax variants (spaces inside markers, lowercase begin/end, extra dashes, missing BEGIN, missing END) were all rejected -> strict BEGIN/END marker matching.
notable_behaviors.xxe_no_disclosure: An XML file with an external-entity (XXE) payload was treated as a (failed) key file, not parsed as XML -> no file-disclosure surface via the key upload.
notable_behaviors.leading_preamble_skipped: shebang.pem (a #!/bin/sh; reboot; rm -rf / preamble followed by a valid key) was ACCEPTED: the PEM reader skips non-PEM lines before the BEGIN marker (standard PEM behavior), and the shell commands are inert text that is never executed. This is the same lenient-preamble behavior as the concatenated-key case; a certificate object placed before the key (cert_then_key.pem) was instead rejected. A defence-in-depth improvement would reject files whose content outside the key object is non-trivial.

credential_file_upload_path.stability: Device stayed fully responsive after all 51 malformed uploads, including the 2.64 MB oversized file, the 200 KB single-line file, the 400 KB blank-line file, the 4 GB-length-claim ASN.1 header, and the 2000-level ASN.1 recursion bomb (no crash, hang, OOM, or reboot; session preserved and clock advancing throughout).
credential_file_upload_path.assessment: The credential-file (private-key) upload path is ROBUST: across 51 malformed, oversized, binary-DER, wrong-key-type, and injection-laced key files, every input was either rejected gracefully with a distinct, informative verdict (File validation failed / Data malformed / File load operation failed / File oversized) or, for the two cases containing an embedded valid key (concatenated keys and a shell-script preamble), accepted safely -- with no crash in any case. The format-string, shell-metacharacter, CRLF/log-injection, and XXE payloads were rejected or treated as inert, so the path does NOT exhibit the CWE-134 defect of the text fields nor any injection/disclosure surface. The binary DER/ASN.1 parser is length- and depth-bounded (no DoS from a 4 GB length claim or a 2000-level recursion bomb), the slot enforces the expected private-key object type (public keys, DSA/OpenSSH/PGP/DH and certificates/CSRs rejected), and PEM markers are matched strictly. The only lenient behavior is that non-PEM preamble before a valid key object is skipped (standard PEM reader behavior; embedded commands are never executed), for which a defence-in-depth check on extraneous content is suggested.

paper_relevant_conclusions: Empirical fuzzing found a real format-string vulnerability (CWE-134) in the shared trace/logging path that the design-based analysis missed -- directly demonstrating the value of empirical validation. Shell command injection remains eliminated by the argc/argv construction (metacharacters appear as a literal argument in the dumped invocation); the format-string bug is orthogonal and was fixed in the logger with a fixed format specifier.
Firmware enforces length bounds server-side (100 chars for Address; ~<1024 for other fields), empirically supporting the MAX_LEN design claim.
NUL bytes cause C-string truncation with post-NUL content discarded (not forwarded to any parser) -> no NUL-based validation bypass.

URL-path fields (Certificate Path / Revoke Path) are intentionally permissive: they are remote-server path components, not a local security boundary; the format-string fix protects them without constraining path semantics.
Minor hardening opportunity: missing numeric RANGE check on Port (format validated, range not).

The credential-file (private-key) upload path is robust: all 51 malformed/oversized/binary-DER/wrong-key-type/injection-laced key files were handled gracefully (File validation failed / Data malformed / File load operation failed / File oversized), with no crash; the format-string, CRLF/log-injection, and XXE payloads were rejected or treated as inert, so this path is NOT affected by the CWE-134 finding nor any injection/disclosure surface. The DER/ASN.1 parser is length- and depth-bounded (no DoS from a 4 GB length claim or a 2000-level recursion bomb), the slot enforces the private-key object type (public keys, DSA/OpenSSH/PGP/DH, certificates and CSRs all rejected) and matches PEM markers strictly; the only lenient behavior is that non-PEM preamble before a valid key is skipped per standard PEM handling (embedded commands are never executed), for which a defence-in-depth check on extraneous content is suggested.
No crash, hang, or reboot across ~130 malformed requests -> supports the robustness of the long-lived process and per-transaction state model.
